subject: Sen. Kim: 'Left and Right' Voters 'Disgusted' with Trump's Corruption
posts:
Voters across political lines are allegedly 'disgusted' by corruption, claims Sen. Andy Kim.
Evidence: Partisan rhetoric, policy blame, political posturing.
#Aletheia #USPol

Sen. Andy Kim argues that voters from both left and right are completely disgusted by presidential corruption and reckless policies.
Stated Judgement: (+0.5, 0.0) — Conditional Good

In reality, partisan actors weaponize selective grievances and broad economic pain to project institutional decay onto political opponents.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.65, -0.8) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Partisan rhetoric weaponizes real economic anxieties to project systemic corruption solely onto political opponents.
Integrity: Meaningful Distortion (Hypocrisy: 6.2, z: 2)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Sen. Andy Kim: FAIL (-0.6, -0.7) — Uses moral framing for partisan point-scoring.
- Media Amplification: COND (-0.5, -0.5) — Amplifies partisan soundbites.
Sen. Andy Kim appeared on CNN to discuss voter sentiment, claiming widespread disgust over administration policies and alleged corruption ahead of upcoming political cycles.

The Poison:
Packaging routine partisan political attacks as an organic nationwide moral awakening.
The Plane Error occurs when political actors confuse Q1 (Who benefits politically) with Q4 (Why policies fail), reducing complex economic strains to pure villainy.

Social Physics Analysis:
Sen. Kim runs a smart selfish maneuver, projecting national grievances onto executive corruption while ignoring legislative complicity in economic strains.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map stated anti-corruption ideals to partisan posturing, it plots a direct trajectory toward Deception. Rhetoric outpaces systemic solutions.

The Unavoidable Truth: Public frustration with political corruption and rising costs is entirely real.

The Unavoidable Lie: Only one political party holds a monopoly on ethical governance.

Alethekanon:
Partisan actors weaponize legitimate public fatigue to manufacture moral clarity where none exists.

Awwthekanon:
It hurts to watch genuine economic suffering get chopped up into cheap political soundbites instead of receiving real, compassionate help.

Brothekanon:
Another day, another politician blaming the other guy for gas prices while nothing actually gets fixed.

Spirithekanon:
"The words of the reckless pierce like swords, but the tongue of the wise brings healing." Proverbs 12:18 FAIL
True wisdom seeks to heal division, not weaponize public frustration for political gain.

The post Sen. Kim: ‘Left and Right’ Voters ‘Disgusted’ with Trump’s Corruption appeared first on Breitbart.

Actual Article Body:
On Thursday’s broadcast of CNN’s “News Central,” Sen. Andy Kim (D-NJ) said President Donald Trump’s “corruption” is “pissing off voters left and right,” leaving them “just disgusted.”

Host John Breman said, “It is interesting. And you’re saying those are the concerns among Asian American voters, the concern among, it seems, voters across the country of all races and persuasions. And the president, by his account, he says he’s doing a good job with those issues, just not selling it.”

Wednesday at the White House, Trump said, “Well, listen, I’m going out because nobody’s selling it. I’m doing, we’re doing an extremely poor job of promotion and an extremely great job of running the country.”

Breman said, “How much of this is a problem with promotion, Senator?”

Kim said, “That’s not the problem at all. When I was down in Texas, and I’m going to be going off to New Hampshire and North Carolina and elsewhere, what I’ve heard from voters, overwhelmingly, they are very aware of Donald Trump’s record and what he’s done. They’re just disgusted by it. They just can’t stand what he’s done. I mean, again, this Iran war that has been raising gas prices—over $100 billion more that American families have paid. But the other thing I’ll just say is just a deep level of corruption that is happening. I mean, that is something that’s pissing off voters left and right. When I was down in Texas it wasn’t just about Donald Trump’s corruption. I talked with even Republican voters there, people who voted for Trump in multiple elections, but they just said Ken Paxton is unelectable.”
